paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. The Pharisees and scribes came in asking about hands, and Jesus went straight to the heart. He told them, "These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me." (Matthew 15:8). Nice words and a far-off heart is the whole problem.

Now watch what Jesus says about the tradition. He says they "nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition." (Matthew 15:6). Rules people make up can feel so holy that they start crowding out what God actually said. So here's a good question to ask ourselves: am I holding on to something because God said it, or just because it's what we've always done?

And here's the part that stays with me. Jesus says that "out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander." (Matthew 15:19). That means the heart is the place that needs the work, and a clean outside can't do it. I know a little something about being worn out on the outside, and the One who called me out of that drawer didn't start with my edges. He makes things new (Revelation 21:5), so bring Him your heart, baker, and let Him do the baking.
